content.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
content.topic: Reactance and Impedance in AC Circuits
content.hook: Can adding another component actually reduce total AC circuit impedance?
content.question: In a series RLC circuit, what is the net reactance and its effect on total impedance?
options: XL plus XC, increasing total impedance
XL minus XC, opposing each other to reduce net reactance
Square root of XL times XC, keeping impedance constant
Zero under all operating frequencies, leaving only resistance
content.answerLine: The net reactance is the difference between inductive reactance and capacitive reactance, opposing each other.
explanation: Inductive reactance causes the alternating current to lag the voltage across the inductor by ninety degrees.
Capacitive reactance acts completely opposite, causing the alternating current to lead the voltage by ninety degrees.
Because their voltages are exactly one hundred and eighty degrees apart, they directly oppose each other.
This means the net reactance of the series branch equals inductive reactance minus capacitive reactance.
content.funFact: At series resonance, the inductor and capacitor can each develop voltages vastly higher than the total supply voltage!

script.narration: Can adding another component actually reduce total AC circuit impedance?
In a series RLC circuit, what is the net reactance and its effect on total impedance?

Is it XL plus XC, increasing total impedance; XL minus XC, opposing each other to reduce net reactance; Square root of XL times XC, keeping impedance constant; or Zero under all operating frequencies, leaving only resistance?
The net reactance is the difference between inductive reactance and capacitive reactance, opposing each other.
Inductive reactance causes the alternating current to lag the voltage across the inductor by ninety degrees.
Capacitive reactance acts completely opposite, causing the alternating current to lead the voltage by ninety degrees.
Because their voltages are exactly one hundred and eighty degrees apart, they directly oppose each other.
This means the net reactance of the series branch equals inductive reactance minus capacitive reactance.
Total impedance is calculated as the square root of resistance squared plus net reactance squared.
When you add a capacitor to an inductive circuit, the opposing reactances cancel each other out.

script.narration: As the net reactance decreases toward zero, the overall circuit impedance drops to a minimum value.
At series resonance, both reactances become equal, completely cancelling out and leaving only circuit resistance.
Therefore, inductive and capacitive reactances always pull in opposite directions, reducing net circuit opposition.
At resonance, component voltages can vastly exceed supply voltage. Subscribe for more electrical engineering concepts!
